title: Matrix-chain ordering: plain recursion vs dynamic programming
problem_statement: Given dimensions p_0, ..., p_n of a chain of n matrices (matrix i is p_(i-1) x p_i), compute the minimum number of scalar multiplications needed to evaluate the product, over all parenthesisations.

algorithms.name: plain recursion
algorithms.idea: Try every top-level split point k and recurse on both halves, without memoisation.
algorithms.pseudocode: cost(i, j) = 0 if i = j else min over k of cost(i, k) + cost(k+1, j) + p_(i-1) p_k p_j
algorithms.correctness: Optimal substructure (CLRS 15.2). Running time: T(n) = sum_k (T(k) + T(n-k)) + Theta(n) gives T(n) - T(n-1) = 2 T(n-1) + Theta(1), so T(n) = Theta(3^n). CLRS proves the weaker Omega(2^n).

algorithms.name: bottom-up dynamic programming
algorithms.idea: Fill m[i][j] for increasing chain length; each of the Theta(n^2) cells takes a min over O(n) split points.

relationship: Plain recursion is Theta(3^n) (full enumeration of parenthesisations would be Catalan, ~4^n / n^1.5); memoising the Theta(n^2) subchains gives Theta(n^3). Hu and Shing (1982, 1984) published an O(n log n) algorithm (not implemented or verified here). Schwartz & Weiss (2019) report that its original correctness proof is wrong; their abstract states that they 'present an alternative proof for the correctness of the first two algorithms' they discuss.

sources.authors: Cormen, T. H.; Leiserson, C. E.; Rivest, R. L.; Stein, C.
sources.title: Introduction to Algorithms (3rd ed.)

sources.authors: Hu, T. C.; Shing, M. T.
sources.title: Computation of Matrix Chain Products. Part II
Revisiting "Computation of Matrix Chain Products"
sources.note: Only the abstract (Crossref record) was consulted. It states that the correctness proof of Hu and Shing's O(N log N) algorithm is wrong and that the authors present an alternative proof for the correctness of the first two algorithms.

verification.method: V1: both agree on random chains with dimensions in [1, 50] (n <= 10 for recursion) and respect an independent upper bound. V2: runtimes fitted against 3^n and n^3.

caveats: Dimensions are small integers, so arithmetic is unit cost.
notes: Hu and Shing published an O(n log n) algorithm (on its correctness proof see Schwartz & Weiss 2019 in the relationship); it is not implemented or verified in this entry.
